entries.sense_en: in the middle of; surrounded by

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and neutral; midst sounds literary or formal.
synonyms.example: in the middle of the room

synonyms.nuance: One word, also formal; often used for noise, events or feelings around you.
Surrounded by several separate things, not a single space or mass.

entries.tip_ko: midst는 끝의 -dst 자음이 몰려 있어요: /mɪdst/ '미드스트'를 한 음절로.

entries.sense_en: warm, safe and comfortable, often in a small space

synonyms.nuance: Warm and pleasant, especially a room or atmosphere; the most common everyday word.
General physical ease; no sense of being small, sheltered or warm.
Protected from wind, weather or danger; no idea of warmth.

entries.tip_ko: snug는 옷이 '꼭 맞는'이라는 뜻으로도 써요: a snug fit.

entries.sense_en: a quiet, private place where you can hide or rest

synonyms.nuance: Informal; stresses that the place is secret or hard to find.
A place of safety from danger or trouble, not just for peace and quiet.
synonyms.example: They found refuge in a church.

synonyms.nuance: Literary; a safe, peaceful place, often used figuratively.

entries.tip_ko: retreat는 흔히 '후퇴(하다)'예요. 여기서는 '숨어 쉬는 곳'이라는 명사예요.

entries.sense_en: a group of young birds hatched at the same time by one mother

synonyms.nuance: Young mammals born together, such as puppies or kittens, not birds.
The set of eggs laid together, before they hatch.
Formal, general word for anyone's children or young, not a group born together.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 brood는 '곰곰이 괴로워하며 생각하다'라는 전혀 다른 뜻이에요: brood over a mistake.

entries.sense_en: (of a baby bird) to come out of its egg

synonyms.nuance: Technical; keeping eggs warm until they hatch, not the moment of coming out.
General word for coming out of anything; not specific to eggs.
synonyms.example: A butterfly emerged from the cocoon.

synonyms.nuance: For mammals born from a mother's body; hatch is only for eggs.
synonyms.example: The calf was born at night.

entries.tip_ko: hatch a plan은 '(몰래) 계획을 꾸미다'라는 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: to go somewhere even though it might be risky or unfamiliar

synonyms.nuance: Stresses courage to do something frightening; not specifically about going somewhere.
Focuses on the possible loss or danger, not the journey.
To go somewhere without purpose; no sense of danger or boldness.
synonyms.example: We wandered into the old town.

entries.sense_en: a village priest or minister in charge of a church

synonyms.nuance: General word, especially Catholic or Orthodox clergy.
Common today, especially in American Protestant churches.
British; the priest of a Church of England parish.

entries.sense_en: an old exclamation of surprise or annoyance

synonyms.nuance: Also old-fashioned; shows mild shock or amazement.
Gentle, a little old-fashioned, but still heard today.
Modern and very common for mild surprise.
synonyms.example: Oh my, look at the time.

entries.tip_ko: declare의 보통 뜻은 '선언하다, (세관에) 신고하다'예요.

entries.sense_en: to look exactly like someone, especially a parent

synonyms.nuance: The most common modern form; informal and emphatic.
synonyms.example: She's the spitting image of her mom.

synonyms.nuance: Resemble a parent in looks or character, not only appearance.
Plain and neutral; can mean only a partial resemblance.

entries.sense_en: to make someone agree to do something by giving reasons

synonyms.nuance: Usually about making someone believe something is true; persuade is about getting them to act.
synonyms.example: I convinced him I was right.

synonyms.nuance: Informal; suggests the person was reluctant at first.
Gently and patiently, with kind words.
synonyms.example: He coaxed the cat out from under the bed.

entries.tip_ko: persuade someone to do (행동하게 설득), convince someone that (믿게 하다)로 구별해요.

entries.sense_en: without any result; uselessly

synonyms.nuance: Also formal; the standard phrase for effort that fails.
Informal; often sounds bitter about wasted effort.
Formal, common in writing and news.
synonyms.example: Doctors tried, but to no avail.

entries.modern: to no purpose → in vain / for nothing

entries.sense_en: do what you want (said when you don't care or mildly disapprove)

synonyms.nuance: The most common version today; sounds a bit cold or offended.
Neutral and friendly; leaves the decision to the other person.
synonyms.example: Pizza or pasta? It's up to you.

synonyms.nuance: Very informal, can sound rude or bored.

entries.tip_ko: please는 여기서 '제발'이 아니라 '기쁘게 하다'라는 동사예요.

entries.sense_en: out into view; forward

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; forth sounds old or formal.
Toward the front or ahead, not out of something.
Continuing to move ahead in space or time.

entries.tip_ko: back and forth(앞뒤로 왔다 갔다)에서는 지금도 자주 써요. fourth(넷째)와 발음이 같아요.

entries.sense_en: to put your foot on something; step on

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase; tread is more literary or British.
To step on repeatedly and crush or damage.
To bring your foot down hard, often in anger.

entries.tip_ko: 불규칙 변화: tread – trod – trodden.

entries.sense_en: to sharpen something by rubbing it

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word for making any edge or point sharp.
To sharpen on a stone; figuratively, to perfect a skill.
To rub hard to wear down or crush, not only to sharpen.

entries.tip_ko: whet your appetite(식욕·호기심을 돋우다)로 지금도 자주 써요. wet(젖은)과 발음이 같아요.

entries.sense_en: over there, at a distance you can see or point to

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern phrase.
Just far away, with no idea of pointing to it.
Simply points to something; no sense of distance.

entries.modern: that old duck yonder → that old duck over there

entries.sense_en: having good manners because of a good upbringing

synonyms.nuance: Only about polite behavior; says nothing about family or class.
Elegant and cultured in taste and speech.
Everyday word for courteous behavior at a given moment.

entries.tip_ko: 반대말은 ill-bred(버릇없는)예요. 동물에 쓰면 '혈통 좋은'이라는 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: strange or odd

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word for something unusual.
Strange in a slightly uncomfortable way.
Informal, strongly strange.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 queer는 주로 성소수자를 가리키는 말이라 '이상한'의 뜻으로는 거의 쓰지 않아요.

entries.sense_en: wanting to hurt or upset others on purpose

synonyms.nuance: Informal, everyday word for unkind behavior.
synonyms.example: Don't be mean to your brother.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more formal; a real intention to cause harm.
Wanting revenge for something done to you.

entries.sense_en: to force someone to leave a place

synonyms.nuance: Informal and more forceful; common today.
synonyms.example: He was thrown out of the bar.

synonyms.nuance: Formal; officially removing someone from a school or organization.
Very informal and blunt.

entries.tip_ko: turn out은 보통 '~로 판명되다'예요: It turned out to be true. 여기서는 '내쫓다'라는 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: a person's natural character or usual mood

synonyms.nuance: Inborn emotional nature, especially how easily someone gets upset.
Plain, everyday word for basic character.
The whole set of traits others notice; more modern and general.

entries.modern: a very good disposition → a very good nature

entries.sense_en: a male duck

synonyms.nuance: General word for the bird; also specifically the female.
A male goose, not a duck.
A male chicken.

entries.sense_en: farm birds such as chickens, ducks and turkeys

synonyms.nuance: Older or technical word; can mean a single bird or wild birds too.
Only one kind of bird; poultry covers all farm birds.
All farm animals, including cows and pigs.

entries.tip_ko: poultry는 셀 수 없는 집합명사예요: a poultry (X). 발음은 '포울트리'.

entries.sense_en: a sharp, hard point on the back of a male bird's leg

synonyms.nuance: A sharp nail on the toes of an animal, not on the back of the leg.
A large claw of a bird of prey, such as an eagle.
A sharp point on a plant.

entries.tip_ko: spur는 말 탈 때 신발 뒤축에 다는 '박차'도 뜻해요. on the spur of the moment = 충동적으로.

entries.sense_en: to imagine or believe something about yourself, often wrongly

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; to form a picture in your mind, true or not.
Plain modern phrase for self-image.
synonyms.example: He thinks of himself as a genius.

synonyms.nuance: To guess something is probably true.

entries.modern: fancied himself an emperor → thought he was an emperor
entries.tip_ko: 영국 구어 fancy는 '~하고 싶다, 좋아하다'예요: Fancy a coffee?

entries.sense_en: strong anger

synonyms.nuance: Very strong, often uncontrolled anger.
Wild, violent anger; slightly more literary than rage.
A tendency to get angry quickly; lose your temper.

entries.modern: red with passion → red with rage
entries.tip_ko: passion은 보통 '열정'이에요. 옛글에서는 '격한 분노'라는 뜻으로도 써요: in a passion = 화가 나서.

entries.sense_en: a fence made of pointed wooden stakes

synonyms.nuance: Modern term for a low fence of pointed white boards.
A row of bushes used as a fence, not wood.
A fence of metal or wooden bars, often along stairs or a balcony.

entries.sense_en: a wide, open area of wild, wet land

synonyms.nuance: Low land that is soft and wet, often near water.
Wet land with trees; sounds darker and muddier.
Open, dry wild land with low bushes.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 moor는 '배를 정박시키다'라는 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: a tall grass-like plant that grows in wet places

synonyms.nuance: Taller, with hollow stems; very similar and often confused.
A grass-like wetland plant with solid, three-sided stems.
General word for low green plants.

entries.tip_ko: rush는 보통 '서두르다, 돌진'이에요. 여기서는 식물 이름이에요.

entries.sense_en: rude and too bold, but in a lively, amusing way

synonyms.nuance: British, informal; playfully disrespectful.
Formal; rude and disrespectful, not amusing.
American, informal; bold and lively, often admired.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 saucy는 '야한, 선정적인'이라는 뜻으로도 자주 써요.

entries.sense_en: a bird that flies to another country each season

synonyms.nuance: The normal scientific or everyday term.
A person who moves from place to place; the figurative sense of bird of passage.
Negative; a person with no settled home or job.

entries.tip_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 '한곳에 머물지 않는 사람, 뜨내기'라는 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: to add a little color to something

synonyms.nuance: To add a light color on purpose, as with hair or glass.
To leave a mark of color that is hard to remove.
Plain, general word, any amount of color.

entries.tip_ko: tinged with sadness(슬픔이 살짝 배인)처럼 감정에도 써요.

entries.sense_en: to look with fierce, angry, shining eyes

synonyms.nuance: To look for a long time; not necessarily angry.
Angry and sulky, often silently.
synonyms.example: He glowered at me across the table.

synonyms.nuance: A quick look, the opposite of a long fierce one.

entries.tip_ko: 명사 glare는 '눈부신 빛'이라는 뜻도 있어요: the glare of the sun.

entries.sense_en: to break or collapse under pressure

synonyms.nuance: General; any damage, not specifically under weight or strain.
Falling down completely, like a building or bridge.
Breaking suddenly with a sharp sound.

entries.tip_ko: give way는 '양보하다'(영국 도로 표지 Give Way)라는 뜻도 있어요.

entries.sense_en: because of; as a result of

synonyms.nuance: The everyday phrase.
Neutral, a bit more formal than because of.
synonyms.example: as a result of the storm

synonyms.nuance: Common in writing and announcements.

entries.sense_en: stop talking; keep quiet

synonyms.nuance: Neutral and plain.
Very informal and rude.
To stop yourself from saying something you want to say.
synonyms.example: I had to bite my tongue.

entries.sense_en: a formal, often sarcastic way to say 'please'

synonyms.nuance: Formal and polite; can also sound cold or sarcastic.
synonyms.example: Be so kind as to close the door.

synonyms.nuance: Formal 'please' in orders; often shows irritation.
Plain and neutral.

entries.modern: have the goodness to hold your tongue → kindly be quiet
entries.tip_ko: 공손한 형식이지만 여기서는 비꼬는 말투예요.

entries.sense_en: sad and without energy or hope

synonyms.nuance: Informal, everyday word for feeling sad.
Stronger; can mean a medical condition.
Sad and without hope; also used for dark weather.

entries.modern: low spirited → down / in low spirits
entries.tip_ko: 반대로 기분이 좋을 때는 in high spirits라고 해요.

entries.sense_en: a strong wish for something you do not have

synonyms.nuance: General strong wish; can be neutral or physical.
Deep, often sad longing lasting a long time; literary.
Strong physical want, especially for food or drugs.

entries.tip_ko: 동사는 long for(~을 갈망하다)예요: long for home.

entries.sense_en: completely silly and unreasonable

synonyms.nuance: Silly enough to laugh at; very common in speech.
Stronger and more formal; so silly it is almost funny.
Mild and gentle; can be affectionate.

entries.sense_en: to spin or turn around quickly

synonyms.nuance: General word for turning around a center, fast or slow.
Light, graceful turning, like a dancer or a small object.
Moving in twisting curves, like water or smoke.

entries.tip_ko: give it a whirl = 한번 해 보다(구어).

entries.sense_en: all the feathers covering a bird's body

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; can mean individual feathers.
One large, showy feather, or a rising cloud of smoke.
Very soft, fine feathers of young birds or under outer feathers.

entries.sense_en: so bright that it almost blinds you

synonyms.nuance: Very bright or very clever; less about hurting your eyes.
Harshly and unpleasantly bright.
Shining with many small flashes of light.

entries.tip_ko: a dazzling smile처럼 '황홀할 만큼 멋진'이라는 뜻으로도 써요.

entries.sense_en: very unusual and strange

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for anything unusual or hard to explain.
Unusual in a way that deserves attention, usually positive.
The only one of its kind.

entries.modern: a singular cry → a strange cry
entries.tip_ko: singular는 보통 문법의 '단수'예요. 여기서는 '기이한'이라는 옛 뜻이에요.

entries.sense_en: unable to control yourself because of a strong emotion

synonyms.nuance: Emotion is too strong to handle; often sadness or gratitude.
Wildly worried or rushed.
Only for great happiness.
synonyms.example: We were overjoyed at the news.

entries.tip_ko: beside himself는 '그 사람 옆에'가 아니라 '감정 때문에 제정신이 아닌'이에요: beside herself with anger.

entries.sense_en: to have to do something because there is no other choice

synonyms.nuance: Everyday, neutral way to say something is necessary.
Stronger; someone or something makes you do it against your will.
Formal; a rule or law demands it.
synonyms.example: Visitors are required to sign in.

entries.tip_ko: I'm much obliged(대단히 감사합니다)라는 옛 인사말도 있어요.

entries.sense_en: to fly clumsily with quick, light wing movements

synonyms.nuance: Bigger, slower up-and-down wing movement.
Moving quickly and lightly from place to place.
Staying in one place in the air.
synonyms.example: A hummingbird hovered by the flower.

entries.tip_ko: 심장이 '두근거리다', 깃발이 '펄럭이다'에도 flutter를 써요.

entries.sense_en: a lack of basic things like food, warmth and shelter

synonyms.nuance: Any difficult living conditions; more common and general.
Lack of money specifically.
Having something taken away or kept from you, like sleep or rights.

entries.tip_ko: privacy(사생활)와 철자가 비슷하지만 뜻이 전혀 달라요.

entries.sense_en: to suffer something painful or difficult for a long time

synonyms.nuance: To accept something painful; often used with can't.
To allow something unpleasant without complaining; less about suffering.
Informal; accepting something annoying.
synonyms.example: How do you put up with him?

entries.sense_en: a group of bushes and small trees growing close together

synonyms.nuance: A single low woody plant.
A small group of trees, often planted and open.
Low plants covering the ground under trees in a forest.

entries.sense_en: to make a soft sound, like dry leaves or paper moving

synonyms.nuance: Sharper, snapping sounds, like a fire.
A smooth sound of something moving quickly through air.
A soft voice; used poetically for leaves or wind.

entries.tip_ko: t는 발음하지 않아요: /ˈrʌsəl/ '러슬'.

entries.sense_en: to suddenly see something, especially at a distance

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word for noticing something.
synonyms.example: I spotted her in the crowd.

synonyms.nuance: Seeing something briefly or suddenly.
synonyms.example: We caught sight of the sea.

synonyms.nuance: Becoming aware of something, not only by seeing.

entries.sense_en: to treat someone cruelly again and again

synonyms.nuance: Repeated cruelty by a stronger person, often at school or work.
Annoying or threatening someone again and again.
Unfair control by a government or powerful group over many people.

entries.tip_ko: prosecute(기소하다)와 헷갈리지 마세요.

entries.sense_en: to think someone is worthless and dislike them strongly

synonyms.nuance: Strong dislike, but not necessarily looking down on someone.
Showing openly that you think someone is worthless.
Informal; thinking you are better than someone.
